ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The image shows a blank 5×5 grid. According to the problem, it is necessary to color some squares so that every horizontal 1×4 rectangle and every vertical 4×1 rectangle contains at least one colored square. In a 5×5 grid, each row has exactly two horizontal 1×4 rectangles: covering columns 1–4, and covering columns 2–5. Similarly, each column has exactly two vertical 4×1 rectangles: covering rows 1–4, and covering rows 2–5. If a certain row has no colored square, then the horizontal 1×4 rectangles in this row will not be covered, so each row must have at least one colored square. Therefore at least 5 colored squares are needed. Likewise, each column must also have at least one colored square. Now prove that 5 is not enough. If exactly 5 colored squares are used, because each of the 5 rows has at least one, each row has exactly one; and because each of the 5 columns has at least one, each column also has exactly one. In a certain row, if there is only one colored square, then it must simultaneously belong to the two horizontal 1×4 rectangles in that row, that is, simultaneously belong to columns 1–4 and columns 2–5, so it can only be in columns 2, 3, 4. Similarly, in a certain column, if there is only one colored square, then it must simultaneously belong to the two vertical 4×1 rectangles in that column, so it can only be in rows 2, 3, 4. But row 1 must have one colored square, and it can only be in columns 2, 3, 4. Suppose the column it is in is a certain column. Since each column has exactly one colored square, the only colored square in that column is in row 1, not in rows 2, 3, 4, which contradicts the requirement that the only colored square in that column must be in rows 2, 3, 4. Therefore 5 colored squares are impossible. So at least 6 are needed. Below is a construction with 6 colored squares: the colored positions are (1,3), (2,1), (2,5), (3,2), (4,4), (5,3). Check by rows: the colored squares in rows 1, 3, 4, 5 are respectively in columns 3, 2, 4, 3, all of which can cover the two horizontal intervals of length 4 in that row; row 2 is colored in columns 1 and 5, respectively covering the two horizontal intervals columns 1–4 and columns 2–5. Check by columns: column 1 has row 2 colored, column 2 has row 3 colored, column 4 has row 4 colored, column 5 has row 2 colored, all of which can cover the two vertical intervals of length 4 in the corresponding column; column 3 is colored in rows 1 and 5, respectively covering the two vertical intervals rows 1–4 and rows 2–5. Therefore the minimum number is 6.

raw_record.question_text: What is the minimum number of cells of a $5 \times 5$ grid that have to be coloured in so that every possible $1 \times 4$ rectangle and every $4 \times 1$ rectangle in the grid has at least one cell coloured in?

method.method_draft: Model the task as a hitting problem on the rows and columns. From the 5x5 grid, note that in each row there are exactly two horizontal 1x4 rectangles, covering columns 1-4 and 2-5; similarly in each column there are exactly two vertical 4x1 rectangles, covering rows 1-4 and 2-5. A row with no coloured cell would leave a horizontal rectangle uncovered, so every row needs at least one coloured cell; likewise every column needs at least one coloured cell. Thus at least 5 cells are needed. To rule out 5, assume exactly 5 cells are used. Then each row and each column has exactly one coloured cell. In a row with only one coloured cell, that cell must be in columns 2, 3, or 4, since it must lie in both horizontal 1x4 rectangles. In a column with only one coloured cell, that cell must be in rows 2, 3, or 4. But the coloured cell in row 1 must lie in columns 2-4, and since its column has only this one coloured cell, it lies in row 1, not rows 2-4, so that column fails the vertical condition. Therefore 5 is impossible, so at least 6 are needed. Then give an explicit colouring with 6 cells, for example at positions (row,column): (1,3), (2,1), (2,5), (3,2), (4,4), (5,3). Check row by row and column by column that every length-4 segment contains at least one coloured cell. Hence the minimum is 6.

在 5×5 方格中，每一行恰好有两个横向 1×4 矩形：覆盖第 1–4 列，以及覆盖第 2–5 列。类似地，每一列恰好有两个纵向 4×1 矩形：覆盖第 1–4 行，以及覆盖第 2–5 行。

如果某一行没有染色格，那么这一行中的横向 1×4 矩形都不会被覆盖，所以每一行至少要有一个染色格。因此至少需要 5 个染色格。同理，每一列也至少要有一个染色格。

现在证明 5 个不够。若恰好使用 5 个染色格，因为 5 行每行至少一个，所以每行恰好一个；又因为 5 列每列至少一个，所以每列也恰好一个。

在某一行中，如果只有一个染色格，那么它必须同时属于该行的两个横向 1×4 矩形，即同时属于第 1–4 列和第 2–5 列，所以它只能在第 2、3、4 列。同理，在某一列中，如果只有一个染色格，那么它必须同时属于该列的两个纵向 4×1 矩形，所以它只能在第 2、3、4 行。

因此最小数量是 6。
